title: Slide 1 · Finding evidence in text and graphs
question: Ava’s reservation names camera C4. One record gives C4’s shelf and another gives its public pickup desk. If Ava is on her way to collect it, which record belongs with the reservation?
answer: The pickup record. It matches both the item, C4, and the relationship the question asks about.

title: Slide 2 · What would count as evidence?
question: If you kept only the reservation record, which part of Ava’s question could you answer?
answer: You could identify C1 as her camera. Finding the desk still requires a record about C1’s pickup location.

title: Slide 3 · Rank passages by words they share
question: If you added “camera” to P1, would a score of three prove that Ava reserved C1?
answer: No. It would give P1 three matching words. Evidence connecting Ava to C1 still has to come from a reservation record.

title: Slide 4 · Follow a relation in the right direction
question: Suppose Ava reserves C2 and the only pickup link is still for C1. What does this lookup return?
answer: It prints no desk. The second link must begin at C2 to complete a path from Ava’s reservation.

title: Slide 5 · Carry record IDs into the answer
question: Another student says the pickup location is East Desk and cites only R4. Which part can you check with R4?
answer: R4 identifies Ava’s reserved item. To settle the disagreement about location, inspect D8, which gives West Desk for that item.

title: Slide 6 · Score a passage by its overlapping words
question: Replace this line: query = set("camera c1 pickup".split()) with: query = set("c1 west".split()) What will print?
answer:
P1 2
P2 0
P1 contains both c1 and west. P2 contains neither word.

title: Slide 8 · From this module to the next
question: A draft based on a pickup record says “Collect C4 at South Desk and bring a photo ID.” Which part needs a second kind of evidence?
answer: The ID requirement needs a relevant policy record. The pickup record can support the desk location while leaving that other claim open.

title: Office hours · Why retrieve records when the desk already has a graph?
question: Why retrieve records when the desk already has a graph?
answer: A graph helps when the fact you want has a named relation, such as pickup_at. Some instructions may exist only in a note. Retrieving the note lets a student read its wording and decide whether it applies.

title: Office hours · Does an empty graph result mean the item has no pickup desk?
question: Does an empty graph result mean the item has no pickup desk?
answer: An empty result means the records you searched do not give a complete path. The campus could still have a pickup desk whose record is missing. Report what you searched and which link you still need.

title: Exercise 1
question: Mia reserves tripod T2. T2 is stored in Room 1 and collected in Room 4. Write the two graph links needed for “Where do I collect my tripod?”
answer: Mia → reserves → T2 and T2 → pickup_at → Room 4. Following both produces Room 4. The storage link answers a different question.

title: Exercise 2
question: For the query “pickup lens L2”, P1 says “lens L2 collection” and P2 says “pickup lens L3”. Compute both scores and propose a way to distinguish them.
answer: Each scores two. P1 matches lens and L2. P2 matches pickup and lens. Require the requested item ID before ranking, then inspect whether “collection” describes pickup.

title: Exercise 3
question: Kai reserves C1 and T2. Both have pickup links. Why could a working graph lookup still give a misleading one-desk answer?
answer: Both paths may be valid. If Kai asks specifically for the camera, restrict the item to a camera before following pickup_at. If the item is unspecified, give both item–desk pairs or ask which item Kai means.

title: Lab case 1 · Same words, different item
question: Which passage wins on this score? Which mentions the intended item?
answer: The score ties at two. P1 shares C1 and pickup. P2 shares camera and pickup. Only P1 mentions C1.

title: Lab case 2 · One changed edge
question: Where does the path end, and which records did you use?
answer: It ends at East Desk. R4 leads from Ava to C2 and D9 leads from C2 to East Desk. D8 describes C1.

title: Lab case 3 · A missing relation
question: What can the desk tell Ava?
answer: It can confirm the C1 reservation from R4. The pickup location is unknown. S2 would answer a question about storage.
